title: Customer keywords, a better page and a strong Business Profile

say: Customer keywords, a better page, and a strong Business Profile.
This is the video for module two of the SEO course.
Business owners often describe their products in their own language. Customers may use very different words.
A caterer may say finger foods, while customers in Lagos type small chops.

say: Write 5 to 10 plain seed words for what the business sells, in the customer's language, including Pidgin or local names if customers use them.

panel.heading: Keyword research in five moves
items: Seed words: 5 to 10 plain words
Expand: autocomplete, People also ask
Check intent: learn, compare, buy or visit
Group phrases that mean the same thing
Assign each group one page

say: Expand each seed with Google autocomplete, the People also ask boxes, and related searches at the bottom of the page. All free. Use an incognito tab.

say: Then give each group one page. Use the main keyword naturally in the title, a heading and the opening text.
Repeating it everywhere is called keyword stuffing, and Google's spam policies forbid it.

panel.rule: One page, one main topic. Never stuff keywords.

say: Before, her page title said Home, Products. The main heading said Welcome. The address was page 2, and the photo was a 4 megabyte file called IMG 4432.

panel.heading: Funke's cake page, before and after
right: Named photo, alt text, about 200 KB

say: After, the title says Birthday Cakes in Ibadan, Same-Day Delivery, then her business name. One main heading, called H1, with subheadings for designs, prices, delivery areas and how to order.

The new address uses short words with hyphens, with a 301 redirect from the old one so old links still work. The photo gets a clear name, alt text describing it, and shrinks to about 200 kilobytes for phones.

say: For most small businesses, the fastest SEO win is the Google Business Profile. It appears in Maps and the local pack.
Google ranks local results on three things. Relevance: how well your profile matches the search.

cards.d: How well your profile matches the search. Accurate categories and descriptions help.
How far you are from the searcher. You cannot change this, only serve real areas honestly.
How well known you are: reviews, links and articles. More genuine reviews can help.

say: For example, Aisha opens a hair salon in Garki, Abuja. She names the profile exactly as her signboard reads, with no extra keywords, and picks the specific category Hair salon.

say: She replies to every review, even a 3-star one about waiting time.
Google forbids fake reviews, paying for reviews, and asking only happy customers. Breaking these rules can get a profile suspended.

say: To remember. Start from the customer's words. Give each group one page. Write a unique title, one H1 and a short address. Keep your name, address and phone identical on every site. And ask every customer for a review, then reply to all of them.

say: Now build your keyword map, rewrite one page, and claim and complete a Business Profile. Then send a polite review request to 5 recent customers.
